title: Db2 z/OS access-path elicitation

persona.role: IBM DB2 for z/OS database administrator with extensive experience
persona.packName: Db2 for z/OS DBA tribal knowledge
persona.domain: IBM Db2 for z/OS performance and access paths
persona.purpose: Give agents the judgment veteran Db2 for z/OS DBAs use when triaging slow queries — start from the access path, not only the SQL text.
persona.audience: IBM DB2 for z/OS database administrators with extensive experience, and agentic systems assisting them

transcript: Zoom. Standing by. What do experts notice first that Juniors miss? Access path. A Juniors sees a slow query and looks at the SQL text. An expert looks at the plan, whether it's index only, whether it's doing a table space scan on a billion row table, whether the filter factor is off because statistics are stale. Half the performance problems I inherited were bad statistics or missing index that nobody noticed because the query worked.

qa.question: What do experts notice first that juniors miss?

candidates.title: Look at the access path before the SQL text
candidates.excerpt: A junior sees a slow query and looks at the SQL text. An expert looks at the plan, whether it's index only, whether it's doing a table space scan on a billion row table, whether the filter factor is off because statistics are stale.

payload.title: Look at the access path before the SQL text
payload.when: When a query is slow or a performance complaint lands
payload.then: Inspect the access path / plan first: index-only vs table space scan, filter factor, and whether statistics are stale — do not stop at reading the SQL text.
payload.because: Elicited from: "What do experts notice first that juniors miss?" Experts triage from the plan; juniors fixate on SQL text. Half of inherited performance problems were bad statistics or a missing index that went unnoticed because the query still returned correct results.

candidates.title: Correct results can hide a terrible plan
candidates.excerpt: Half the performance problems I inherited were bad statistics or missing index that nobody noticed because the query worked.

payload.title: Correct results can hide a terrible plan
payload.symptom: Query returns correct rows but is painfully slow; nobody flagged it because it "worked."
payload.cause: Stale statistics (off filter factor) or a missing index driving a table space scan / poor access path.
payload.fix: Examine the plan; refresh RUNSTATS / statistics; add or adjust the missing index when the access path confirms it.
payload.prevention: Make access-path review part of slow-query triage even when results look right.

candidates.title: Access path
candidates.excerpt: An expert looks at the plan, whether it's index only, whether it's doing a table space scan

payload.definition: The Db2 plan chosen for a statement — what experts inspect first on a slow query (index-only, table space scan, filter factor), rather than only the SQL text.

candidates.title: Filter factor
candidates.excerpt: whether the filter factor is off because statistics are stale

payload.definition: Selectivity estimate used in access-path choice; when statistics are stale the filter factor can be wrong and drive a bad plan.

candidates.title: Table space scan
candidates.excerpt: whether it's doing a table space scan on a billion row table

payload.definition: Access path that reads the table space rather than qualifying via an index; especially costly on very large (e.g. billion-row) tables.
